topic: The Magic of Dandelin Spheres: Visualizing Conic Sections
target_audience: High school geometry students or early undergraduates

sections.title: Prerequisites: The Geometry of a Cone
lecture_lines: A right circular cone extends in two directions.
A cutting plane slices through the cone.
This intersection creates a conic section.
animations: Create a cone with vertex at origin, #FFFFFF.
Draw a circular cross-section, #FFFF00. Label as 'base'.
Show height and radius, #00FFFF. Label 'h' and 'r'.

sections.title: Introducing the Dandelin Spheres
lecture_lines: Place a sphere inside the cone.
It touches the cone at a circle.
It touches the plane at one point.
We call this point a focus.
Dandelin spheres reveal hidden conic geometry.
animations: Insert a sphere inside the cone, #FF00FF.
Tangent to the cone and the plane, #00FF00.

sections.title: Connecting the Geometry to the Conic
lecture_lines: Points on the conic relate to foci.
Tangency points define key geometric properties.
These spheres prove the conic definition.
animations: Show intersection of plane and cone, #FF0000.
Connect F1, F2 to point P, #FFFFFF.

sections.title: The Visual Transformation
lecture_lines: Tilt the plane to change the shape.
The circle transforms into an ellipse.
Steeper cuts create parabolas and hyperbolas.
Spheres shift to match the new slice.
Every cut maintains its fundamental property.
animations: Animate plane tilting to cut cone, #FFFFFF.

sections.title: Conclusion and Application
lecture_lines: They appear throughout our physical universe.
